content: The most common reason an SIP debit fails is insufficient bank balance on the debit date. Other reasons: an expired or cancelled mandate, or a mandate limit lower than the SIP amount.
source_name: Aditya Birla Sun Life MF - SIP instalment failed: reasons, charges

topic: Bank charges on a failed debit
content: Mutual funds generally don't charge for a missed SIP, but banks may charge a bounce/return fee, commonly ₹100-₹750 plus GST per failed debit (e.g. ₹500 + 18% GST = ₹590 at ICICI Bank). Charges vary by bank.
source_name: Aditya Birla Sun Life MF - SIP instalment failed: reasons, charges

content: Under SEBI's uniform rule (from 1 April 2024), a monthly SIP is cancelled automatically after 3 consecutive failed debits. The AMC/RTA informs the investor after the first failure.
source_name: Taurus MF - FAQs on uniform SIP cancellation (SEBI rule)

topic: How to skip an instalment on Groww
content: On Groww: My SIPs > select the SIP > Edit SIP > Skip Installment. You can skip one instalment at a time and request another skip only after the skipped date has passed.
source_name: Groww help - how to skip an SIP instalment

content: On Groww, an SIP is cancelled automatically if 3 instalments in a row are skipped or missed.

topic: How to change SIP amount or date on Groww
content: On Groww: My SIPs > select the SIP > Edit SIP > Edit Amount & Date.
source_name: Groww blog - how to edit an SIP

content: If the next instalment is within 2 working days, an edit or skip request won't apply to that instalment; it applies from the following one. Acting about a week before the SIP date leaves enough time.
source_name: Groww help - when can I edit my SIP

content: Groww Autopay mandates support skip instalment, step-up SIP and editing date/amount. Older biller mandates need to be upgraded to Groww Autopay to use these features.
source_name: Groww blog - biller mandate discontinued, Groww Autopay

content: An autopay mandate has a maximum amount. If the SIP amount (or the total of SIPs using that mandate) is higher than the limit, the debit can fail. A limit above your SIP total leaves room to step up later.

content: Your balance is usually highest just after salary arrives, and insufficient balance is the most common cause of failure. Setting the SIP date 2-3 days after your usual salary date leaves room for credit delays.

topic: How the planner suggests an amount
content: Surplus = take-home pay - fixed costs - day-to-day spending - existing SIPs/RDs. A cushion is kept for irregular expenses: the larger of 20% of the surplus or 5% of take-home pay. Of what's left, 100% is suggested for SIPs if you have an emergency fund, 75% if you partly have one, and 50% if you don't (the rest builds the fund). The amount is rounded down to the nearest ₹500. It's a budgeting estimate; you can choose any amount.
A commonly suggested guideline is to keep about 3-6 months of essential expenses in easily accessible savings, so a surprise expense doesn't force you to skip or stop investments.
A skipped instalment means no debit and no units bought that month; the SIP continues the next month. Because no debit is attempted, there's no bounce fee.

content: The minimum SIP amount depends on the fund, often ₹100-₹500, and is shown on the fund page.
source_name: Groww blog - how to edit an SIP

content: A step-up SIP increases the SIP amount periodically, e.g. once a year. It's available with Groww Autopay. Starting with a comfortable amount and stepping up later is one way to avoid failed debits.
source_name: Groww blog - biller mandate discontinued, Groww Autopay

content: If several SIPs debit on the same date, the bank needs the total of all of them that day. Spreading dates or keeping them all just after salary avoids a shortfall.

content: Stopping an SIP cancels future instalments; units already bought stay invested. Skipping pauses only one instalment.
